beats.text: Socotra, an island of unique beauty and mystery, sits 380 kilometres south of the Arabian Peninsula.
beats.say: Socotra, an island of unique beauty and mystery, sits 380 kilometres south of the Arabian Peninsula.

scene.credit: Rod Waddington from Kergunyah, Australia / CC BY-SA 2.0

beats.text: Its landscape is a mix of arid coastal plains and rugged mountains, home to over 37% of its plant species found nowhere else.
beats.say: Its landscape is a mix of arid coastal plains and rugged mountains, home to over 37% of its plant species found nowhere else.

scene.credit: Rod Waddington from Kergunyah, Australia / CC BY-SA 2.0

beats.text: Endemic species like the Dragon's Blood Tree thrive here, their red sap a symbol of the island's isolation.
beats.say: Endemic species like the Dragon's Blood Tree thrive here, their red sap a symbol of the island's isolation.

beats.text: Socotra's history is as intriguing as its geography. From ancient trade routes to modern conflicts, the island's story is complex.
beats.say: Socotra's history is as intriguing as its geography. From ancient trade routes to modern conflicts, the island's story is complex.

beats.text: In 2008, Socotra was recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, celebrating its natural and cultural uniqueness.
beats.say: In 2008, Socotra was recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, celebrating its natural and cultural uniqueness.

scene.credit: Rod Waddington from Kergunyah, Australia / CC BY-SA 2.0

facts.claim: Socotra is home to over 37% of its plant species found nowhere else.
facts.quote: It has 835 vascular plant species, of which 37% are endemic.

facts.claim: Dragon's Blood Trees thrive here, their red sap a symbol of the island's isolation.
facts.quote: The island is known for its exceptional level of endemism, with about 37% of its plant species, 90% of its reptile species, and 95% of its land snail species found nowhere else on Earth.

facts.claim: In 2008, Socotra was recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
facts.quote: In 2008, Socotra was recognised as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
